text: **A clone first.** These are the seller's own sections, exactly as captured. Keep their look and change their words. **A brand section** … when no clone can carry the point. **Leave the point out** if neither fits.
note: duplicate of D1 "When no clone can carry the point…"

text: The home page's hero usually opens the page.
note: Pallet 10-26: the agent opened with a centred product-page hero.

text: Leave out clones that do not help this reader decide: navigation, newsletters, resource lists, general testimonials, and whole case-study articles (they make the page long and move the point down).
Do not place two sections that make the same point.
Every button goes to the one destination the brief names for the offer: clone `cta` slots, brand-section buttons, and the header button.
note: Founder 2026-10-18: the one-destination rule is guidance only (the save check was dropped).

text: They are made from the seller's own header … and they carry what a page for an account needs: the seller's logo, the account's logo, a line for the account and one button.

Use "Header template, one page" for a site with one page, which is the usual page for an account: the account line sits in the centre. Use "Header template, with page menu" only when the site has more than one page: the menu sits in the centre.
write the account's full name after "Prepared for", for example "Prepared for Acme Health". … On a site for several accounts, write a line for the group, or hide it.
When there is none, or the site is for several accounts, set `account_shown` to `false`: that hides the logo and the thin line before it.
Its link (`cta_href`) and its words. Point it at the one destination for the offer.

Use it only on a site made for several accounts or a whole segment, when one of the seller's own pages helps the reader. Never on a site for one account: those links lead the reader away from a page written for them.
note: The only site rule that treats segment pages differently from 1:1 pages.

text: Every site starts with the plain footer (`SiteFooter`) … Use the brand's footer template, or a footer of your own, only when the person asks for the seller's own footer or something richer.
The header, the footer and the one destination for the offer are shared by every page.
